df = s.reset_index()

m = Prophet()
m.fit(train)
fc = m.predict(m.make_future_dataframe(periods=h))
# fc has yhat, yhat_lower, yhat_upper, + one column per component
caption: No index tricks, no frequency setting -- just ds and y

code:
print(list(m.seasonalities))   # ['weekly']
print("default MAE", mae(...))  # 24.2

# Prophet only turns on yearly seasonality
# if training history spans >= 2 years
# ours was 702 days -- just short
caption: Worse than seasonal naive (16.13) -- and the printed seasonalities tell you why

code:
m2 = Prophet(yearly_seasonality=True)
m2.fit(train)

print(list(m2.seasonalities))  # ['yearly', 'weekly']
print("yearly=True MAE", mae(...))  # 6.71
caption: One argument: MAE drops from 24.2 to 6.71 -- beats seasonal naive

code:
m3.add_country_holidays(country_name="US")
# with US holidays MAE 6.48 (noise -- no real holidays here)

cv = cross_validation(m2, initial="400 days",
                       period="90 days", horizon="28 days")
# 4 cutoffs, mean MAE 7.31
caption: Rolling-origin backtest confirms the single window's 6.71 wasn't a fluke
